shots.subject: no-1 gate
steps: Camera as given: composed spot (-3.700, 13.200, 1.835), turned -0.00 degrees; the plate's spot (the slide's start) (-3.700, 12.000, 1.835).

checks.about: The eye stands 1.70 m above the view's floor (height 0.14 m) (allowed 1.5 to 1.9 m for still_life).
The camera is level (tilt -0.00 degrees): the planner never tilts; an overview raises the eye.
Not judged: no-1 gate has no size (give it under the shot's "things").
The lowest story thing is man-2, reaching 0.697 down (limit 0.7); a figure's shoes reach up to 0.012 lower than its feet's point, so it may just make it: confirm with the shot checker.
checks.fix: Bring the camera 0.10 m nearer along its view (or man-2 that much nearer the camera): it may stand at most 7.99 m from man-2's front (its feet are now 8.09 m away).

checks.about: Story things in the button strip (0.45 to 0.95 down) end at: no-1 gate 0.53, brazier 0.74, man-1 0.47, man-2 0.74, man-3 0.60, man-4 0.27, man-5 0.35, man-6 0.52, man-7 0.68 across (limit 0.95).
The story things fill a box 0.61 wide and 0.22 tall (limit 0.8 x 0.5 for crowd); edges: man-4 (left), brazier (right), man-6 (top), man-2 (bottom).
The story things stand together in the street: the loneliest, man-4, is 0.19 m from man-5 (limit 0.3 m between footprints).

The spots that can be worked out before rendering (where the lines meet 0.50, 0.50; middle of no-1 gate 0.53, 0.53; middle of the story things 0.45, 0.60) span 0.09 x 0.10 (the plan keeps them inside 0.3 x 0.4 so the brightest parts and the warm light have room within the rule's 0.4 x 0.5).

In the bottom-left quarter, where the eye enters, the boxes cover: man-1 2.1% (over its 2%), man-3 0.4%, man-4 2.5% (over its 2%), man-5 2.9% (over its 2%), man-6 2.4% (over its 2%), no-1-drum-petrol 1.8% (over its 1%), no-1-drum-diesel 1.9% (over its 1%), no-1-worker-2 0.4% (limit 1% a thing, 2% for a story thing in a crowd shot; a box covers more than the thing in it, so these are upper bounds).
checks.fix: Confirm on the render (the shot checker measures the real outlines); if it holds, move man-1, man-4, man-5, man-6, no-1-drum-petrol, no-1-drum-diesel out of the bottom-left quarter.

checks.about: no-1-worker-2's face or profile shows (it faces 88 degrees from the camera); its head is 19 px tall at 20.00 m (composed spot (end)); the house limit 24 px is invented and untested.

Figures with their backs to the camera, at the nearest camera place along the slide: man-6 7.42 m, man-5 7.52 m, man-7 7.62 m, man-2 8.09 m, man-4 8.25 m, man-3 8.35 m, man-1 8.66 m, no-1-worker-1 17.98 m, no-2-worker-1 18.29 m, no-2-worker-2 21.85 m (at least 6.0 m: a 1.75 m man is a quarter of the frame there; nearest man-6 at composed spot (end)).
Crowd "men at No. 1" from this shot (w1): its long axis makes 87 degrees with the view (at least 60; it spreads 1.9 times as far along it as across).
Crowd "men at No. 1" from view w3 (plate): its long axis makes 87 degrees with the view (at least 60; it spreads 1.9 times as far along it as across).
Crowd "men at No. 1": 2 rows deep from this view (front to back: man-6, man-5, man-7; man-2, man-4, man-3, man-1).

Crowd "men at No. 1": gaps between neighbours' shoulders in a row (0.47 m shoulders): man-5-man-6 0.37 m, man-6-man-7 0.32 m, man-4-man-1 0.62 m, man-1-man-3 0.25 m, man-3-man-2 0.22 m (house range 0.3 to 0.5 m).
checks.fix: Check by eye: man-4-man-1 0.62 m, man-1-man-3 0.25 m, man-3-man-2 0.22 m (a back-row man standing between two of the front row fills a wide gap).

checks.about: Crowd "men at No. 1" from this shot: the closest two heads, man-1 and man-6, are 1.60 head widths apart on screen (at least 1.0, so each head can be counted).
Crowd "men at No. 1": the most hidden figure, man-3, shows about 22% of its box (at least 50%; boxes, so a figure behind a gap between two others shows more than this).
checks.fix: Move man-3 sideways into a gap, or check on the render.

checks.about: The 1.20 m slide brings the nearest painted thing, no-1-drum-diesel (its nearest corner 6.50 m away at the end), 1.185 times nearer; the painting's 2672 rows allow 1.286; the longest slide for it is 1.86 m.
The painted ground at the frame's bottom edge (2.92 m away) comes 1.411 times nearer (not counted: nobody has judged whether its softness shows; --count-ground counts it).

Casting the film frame's corners and edge middles onto the floor every 10% of the slide, the plate needs a lens of at least 63.53 degrees (with the 0.03 fade band at its edge); the house plate lens is 64.4 (film 60.4 + 4.0); the camera may turn 1.38 degrees each way inside it.
For the slide's worst magnification the plate would need 2462 rows of real detail; the painter returns 2672 (the house plate is 1536 x 2730).
